latin: Sonum non ex motu aeris intercepti inter duo corpora se percutientia, ut tenet Aristoteles_et expositores eius, sed ex contactu tali talium uel talium corporum, talem uel talem sonum causari, dico.

translation: I hold that sound is caused not by the motion of the air trapped between two colliding bodies, as Aristotle and his commentators maintain, but by the contact, of such-and-such a kind, of such-and-such bodies, producing such-and-such a sound.
